module.title: Backend Development Fundamentals
module.description: Learn how servers, APIs, databases, and backend systems power modern web applications.

lessons.title: What Is Backend Development?

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Backend development handles the hidden logic, data processing, authentication, and server operations behind applications.

sections.heading: Frontend Cannot Work Alone
sections.content: Frontend only displays interfaces. Real applications also need logic, security, storage, and processing handled by backend systems.

sections.heading: What Backend Actually Does
sections.content: Backend handles user authentication, databases, APIs, business logic, and application processing.

sections.heading: Backend Runs On Servers
sections.content: Backend code runs on servers connected to the internet and responds to user requests.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Depend On Backend
sections.content: Instagram, Netflix, banking apps, ecommerce platforms, and AI systems all rely heavily on backend infrastructure.

easyExample.title: Restaurant Kitchen Example
easyExample.content: Customers only see the dining area, but the kitchen secretly prepares everything. Backend works similarly behind applications.

summary: Modern systems rely on backend infrastructure

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: A server is a computer that receives requests, processes them, and sends responses back to users.

sections.heading: Why Servers Exist
sections.content: Applications need systems that can store data and handle requests from many users simultaneously.

sections.heading: How Servers Work
sections.content: Servers constantly wait for incoming requests from browsers or mobile apps.

sections.heading: Request Processing
sections.content: Servers process requests, run logic, access databases, and return responses.

sections.heading: Servers Power The Internet
sections.content: Every website, application, and online service depends on servers.

easyExample.title: Customer Support Example
easyExample.content: A customer support desk waits for people to ask questions, processes requests, and gives answers. Servers work similarly.

lessons.title: Understanding APIs And Routes

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Routes and APIs define how frontend applications communicate with backend systems.

sections.heading: Why APIs Exist
sections.content: Frontend applications need structured ways to request data and actions from backend systems.

sections.heading: What Is A Route?
sections.content: A route is a specific backend path handling requests like login, products, or users.

sections.heading: How APIs Work
sections.content: Frontend sends requests to API routes and backend returns responses.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Use APIs Constantly
sections.content: Every login, notification, dashboard update, and search request usually involves APIs.

easyExample.title: Hotel Room Example
easyExample.content: Different hotel rooms serve different purposes. Similarly, API routes handle different application tasks.

summary: Modern apps heavily rely on APIs

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: HTTP methods define what action frontend applications want backend systems to perform.

sections.heading: Why Methods Exist
sections.content: Applications need different actions like fetching, creating, updating, and deleting data.

sections.heading: GET Method
sections.content: GET requests are used to retrieve data from backend systems.

sections.heading: POST Method
sections.content: POST requests send new data to backend systems.

sections.heading: PUT And DELETE
sections.content: PUT updates data while DELETE removes data.

easyExample.title: Library Example
easyExample.content: Borrowing a book is like GET, adding a new book is POST, updating book details is PUT, and removing a book is DELETE.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Backend applications process requests and return responses to users.

sections.heading: Frontend Starts Communication
sections.content: Users interact with frontend interfaces which trigger backend requests.

sections.heading: Backend Receives Request
sections.content: Servers receive incoming requests containing data and instructions.

sections.heading: Processing Logic
sections.content: Backend checks authentication, validations, databases, and business logic.

sections.heading: Returning Response
sections.content: Backend sends final results back to frontend applications.

easyExample.title: Online Order Example
easyExample.content: Customers place orders, restaurants process them, and delivery arrives back. Backend request flow works similarly.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Backend architecture organizes application logic into structured systems.

sections.heading: Why Architecture Matters
sections.content: Large applications become difficult to manage without proper organization.

sections.heading: Separating Responsibilities
sections.content: Routes, controllers, middleware, and database logic are usually separated into different files.

sections.heading: Scalable Applications
sections.content: Good architecture helps applications grow without becoming messy.

sections.heading: Professional Backend Development
sections.content: Real companies organize backend systems carefully for maintainability and teamwork.

easyExample.title: Hospital Department Example
easyExample.content: Hospitals divide responsibilities into departments like reception, surgery, and pharmacy. Backend systems organize similarly.
